Quickstart

sand3d 1.6.3

sand3d is a Python library for writing 3D objects as programs. A program calls verbs that make solids, edit them and place them; Blender does the geometry. This page shows every verb with code that runs, the materials a part can be made of, articulations, the 6 rules a program follows, and how to write an assembly.

1"""A chair, written as an assembly: the plan first, then the details, then the parts.2 3`chair` reads as a table of contents. `chair_frame` is the plan: the seat on its legs,4and the anchors the details need. Each `add_` function hangs one detail on those5anchors: delete its line and nothing else moves — without `add_back` it is a stool.6The parts come last, each built at its own origin, standing on z = 0.7"""8import sand3d as s3d9 10 11def chair(width=440, depth=420, seat_h=450):12    chair = chair_frame(width, depth, seat_h)   # the plan13    add_back(chair)                             # the details, on the plan's anchors14    add_rails(chair)15    return chair.root16 17 18# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the plan19 20def chair_frame(width, depth, seat_h, t=30, inset=35):21    """The seat on four legs. Publishes the width, the seat's height and the line22    the back stands on."""23    legs = s3d.at(leg(seat_h - t), on=s3d.grid(2, 2, width - 2 * inset, depth - 2 * inset))24    seat = s3d.at(seat_board(width, depth, t), z=seat_h - t)25    return s3d.assembly("chair", seat, legs, width=width, depth=depth, seat_h=seat_h, inset=inset,26                        back_y=depth / 2 - 20)27 28 29# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the details30 31def add_back(chair, h=420, t=24, button_d=16):32    """A panel standing on the seat's back edge, buttoned on its face."""33    back = s3d.at(back_panel(chair.width - 40, h, t), y=chair.back_y, z=chair.seat_h)34    # a side face's frame starts at z = 0, below the parent's origin, and its Y is up35    face = back.face("-Y").move(y=chair.seat_h + h * 0.6)36    buttons = s3d.at(s3d.dome("button", button_d, 5), on=s3d.grid(3, 2, 100, 110, on=face))37    s3d.attach(chair, "back", back, buttons)38 39 40def add_rails(chair, d=18, z=160):41    """A rail between the front and back legs, on each side."""42    # both=True: centred on its middle, so turned about X it spans the depth evenly43    rail = s3d.extrude("rail", s3d.circle(d), chair.depth - 2 * chair.inset, both=True)44    sides = s3d.grid(2, 1, chair.width - 2 * chair.inset, on=s3d.Frame((0, 0, z)))45    s3d.attach(chair, "rails", s3d.at(rail, rx=90, on=sides))46 47 48# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the parts49 50def seat_board(width, depth, t):51    return s3d.fillet(s3d.box("seat", width, depth, t), 8, edges="top")52 53 54def leg(h, foot=26, top=36):55    """Tapered, its foot on z = 0."""56    return s3d.cone("leg", foot, h, d2=top)57 58 59def back_panel(width, h, t):60    return s3d.fillet(s3d.box("back", width, t, h), 6, edges="top")

1"""The weight stack of a cable machine.2 3A column of plates resting in two rubber bumpers, two guide rods standing over the4top plate, and the selector: two nuts and a stem on top, the pin's head at the5chosen plate and a spring lanyard hanging from under the nuts down to it.6 7Millimetres. The stack's frame has its origin under the middle of the lowest8plate, X along the plates, -Y towards the user.9"""10import json11import sys12 13import sand3d as s3d14 15 16# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the object: architecture first, then details17 18def weight_stack(n_plates=14, selected=9):19    """The plates, then each detail on their anchors. Any `add_` line can be deleted:20    the rest of the object does not change."""21    stack = plate_column(n_plates)22    add_bumpers(stack)23    add_guide_rods(stack)24    add_selector(stack, selected)25    return stack.root26 27 28def plate_column(n_plates=14, pitch=24, plate_h=22, plate_d=100, guide_spacing=300):29    """`n_plates` plates `pitch` apart. Publishes where details go: every plate's30    height, the top face, the front face and the two guide lines."""31    bottoms = [i * pitch for i in range(n_plates)]32    plate_z = [z + plate_h / 2 for z in bottoms]33    return s3d.assembly("weight_stack",34                        *[s3d.at(weight_plate(d=plate_d, h=plate_h), z=z) for z in bottoms],35                        plate_z=plate_z, top=bottoms[-1] + plate_h, front=-plate_d / 2,36                        guides=(-guide_spacing / 2, guide_spacing / 2))37 38 39# ---------------------------------------------------------------- details, each on the stack's anchors40 41def add_bumpers(stack, sink=10):42    """Two rubber cups under the guide lines, taking the lowest plate `sink` deep."""43    s3d.attach(stack, "bumpers", *[s3d.at(bumper(), x=x, z=sink, anchor="top") for x in stack.guides])44 45 46def add_guide_rods(stack, gap=8):47    """Two rods on the guide lines, standing `gap` above the top plate."""48    s3d.attach(stack, "guide_rods", *[s3d.at(guide_rod(), x=x, z=stack.top + gap, anchor="bottom")49                                      for x in stack.guides])50 51 52def add_selector(stack, selected=9, nut_t=6, nut_gap=4, head_out=12, lanyard_y=-28):53    """On the top plate, two nuts and the stem; the lanyard's loop sits under the54    upper nut and its spring hangs in front, down to the pin head at plate `selected`."""55    upper = stack.top + nut_t + nut_gap     # under the upper nut56    pinned = stack.plate_z[selected]57    s3d.attach(stack, "selector",58               s3d.at(hex_nut(t=nut_t), z=stack.top, anchor="bottom"),59               s3d.at(hex_nut(t=nut_t), z=upper, anchor="bottom"),60               s3d.at(selector_stem(), z=stack.top),61               s3d.at(pin_head(), y=stack.front - head_out, z=pinned, rx=90),62               s3d.at(spring_lanyard(length=upper - pinned), y=lanyard_y, z=(upper + pinned) / 2, rz=-90))63 64 65# ---------------------------------------------------------------- parts, in the order they are called66 67def weight_plate(w=420, d=100, h=22, hole_d=16, edge_r=2):68    """A steel plate with softened edges, drilled front to back for the selector pin."""69    plate = s3d.fillet(s3d.box("weight_plate", w, d, h), edge_r)70    return s3d.hole(plate, hole_d, on=plate.face("-Y").move(y=h / 2))71 72 73def bumper(d_foot=50, d_mouth=46, h=60, wall=2):74    """A rubber cup the stack rests in, open at the top."""75    cup = s3d.revolve("bumper", [(0, -h / 2), (d_foot / 2, -h / 2), (d_mouth / 2, h / 2), (0, h / 2)])76    return s3d.shell(cup, wall, open="top")77 78 79def guide_rod(d=25, length=900, collar_d=35, collar_h=20):80    """A round rod with a collar at its foot."""81    foot, head = -length / 2, length / 282    return s3d.revolve("guide_rod", [(0, foot), (collar_d / 2, foot), (collar_d / 2, foot + collar_h),83                                     (d / 2, foot + collar_h), (d / 2, head), (0, head)])84 85 86def hex_nut(across_corners=32, hole_d=16.5, t=6):87    return s3d.extrude("hex_nut", s3d.polygon(6, across_corners) - s3d.circle(hole_d), t, both=True)88 89 90def selector_stem(d=15, h=30, wall=1.5):91    """The top of the stem that threads the plates, an open sleeve."""92    return s3d.tube("selector_stem", d, d - 2 * wall, h)93 94 95def pin_head(d=36, t=3, boss_d=12, boss_t=6, hole_d=8):96    """The head of the selector pin, a disc with a boss, facing the user."""97    return s3d.revolve("pin_head", [(hole_d / 2, -boss_t / 2), (boss_d / 2, -boss_t / 2), (boss_d / 2, boss_t / 2 - t),98                                    (d / 2, boss_t / 2 - t), (d / 2, boss_t / 2), (hole_d / 2, boss_t / 2)])99 100 101def spring_lanyard(length=150, loop_d=44, loop_gap=40, neck=40, coil_x=24, lean=12, coil_d=4, wire_d=2.2,102                   pitch=2.6):103    """A loop lying flat on top, round the selector stem and open by `loop_gap`104    degrees, and a close-wound spring hanging `length` down from it, `neck` away105    from the loop's centre and leaning `lean` outwards by its foot."""106    top = length / 2 - wire_d / 2107    loop = s3d.arc((coil_x - neck, 0, top), loop_d / 2, loop_gap / 2, 360 - loop_gap / 2)108    hanging = s3d.at(s3d.helix(coil_d, pitch, 2 * top), x=coil_x, z=top, rx=180)   # from the loop, down109    coil = [(x + lean * (top - 1"""A spoon and a fork, from generic verbs — the regression test for "the vocabulary has a2hole": MeshCoder had to hard-code both.3 4Millimetres; the piece lies along +X from its business end, Z up. r                      # where the round end begins19 20    def place(x, width, thick):21        u = (x - x0) / length22        return s3d.at(s3d.superellipse(width, thick, 4), x=x, y=y0, z=z0 + rise * (3 * u ** 2 - 2 * u ** 3), rz=90)23    sections = []24    for k in range(stations):25        u = k / (stations - 1)26        sections.append(place(x0 + body * u, neck[0] + (end[0] - neck[0]) * u ** 1.6,27                              neck[1] + (end[1] - neck[1]) * u))28    for k in range(1, end_steps + 1):29        a = math.radians(85 * k / end_steps)30        sections.append(place(x0 + body + r * math.sin(a), end[0] * math.cos(a), end[1] * (1 - 0.3 * k / end_steps)))31    return s3d.loft("handle", *sections, follow=True)32 33 34def spoon(bowl=(62, 42), depth=13, wall=1.4, rim_r=0.5):35    """A bowl — half an ellipsoid, hollowed, its rim softened — and the handle."""36    length, width = bowl37    cup = s3d.scale(s3d.sphere("bowl", 1), (length, width, 2 * depth))38    s3d.split(cup, s3d.Frame((0, 0, depth)), keep="below")39    cup = s3d.at(cup, z=-depth)                                        # its rim on z = 040    s3d.shell(cup, wall, open="cut")41    s3d.fillet(cup, rim_r, edges="shell")42    return s3d.join(cup, s3d.at(handle(start=(length / 2 - 3, 0, -wall / 2)), z=0))43 44 45def fork(head=(48, 25), tines=4, gap=2.2, root=17, t=2.2, bend_r=140):46    """A flat head cut into `tines` from its tip back to `root`, bent to a curve by47    keeping what a curved plate shares with it — and the handle."""48    length, width = head49    outline = s3d.poly([(-length, -width / 2), (0, -width / 2 + 3), (8, -4.5), (8, 4.5), (0, width / 2 - 3),50                        (-length, width / 2)], fillet=[4, 0, 3, 3, 0, 4])51    pitch = width / tines52    for k in range(1, tines):53        y = -width / 2 + k * pitch54        outline = outline - s3d.at(s3d.slot(2 * (length - root) + gap, gap), x=-length, y=y)55    prism = s3d.extrude("head", outline, 60, both=True)56    steps = 2457    curve = [(bend_r * math.sin(a), 0, bend_r * (1 - math.cos(a)))       # through the neck, rising to the tips58             for a in (-0.42 + 0.5 * k / steps for k in range(steps + 1))]59    plate = s3d.sweep("bend", s3d.rect(t, 4 * width), curve)60    s3d.intersect(prism, plate)61    return s3d.join(prism, handle(start=(6, 0, -t / 4)))

1import sand3d as s3d2 3 4def gate(w=750, h=1200, post=100):5    l_post = s3d.at(s3d.box("post", post, post, h + 300), x=-w - post / 2)6    r_post = s3d.transform(s3d.copy(l_post), mirror="x")7    board = s3d.at(s3d.box("board", w, 40, h), x=-w / 2, z=150)                    # from the post to x = 08    handle = s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("handle", 20, 60), on=s3d.bbox(board, "+Y").move(x=60 - w / 2))  # near x = 09    leaf = s3d.group("leaf", board, handle)                                        # the handle moves with it10    s3d.joint("hinge", leaf, s3d.bbox(l_post, "+X+Y"), axis="+Z", range=(0, 90))   # the post's edge it opens toward: +X turns toward +Y11    twin = s3d.transform(s3d.copy(leaf), mirror="x")                               # its image, hinged at x = +w: opens toward +Y too12    gate = s3d.assembly("gate", l_post, r_post, leaf, twin)13    s3d.pose(leaf, 60)14    return gate

1"""f03 — a ring notched round its outside, the notches only through its lower half,2their four vertical edges chamfered.3 4Source: Zero-To-CAD-1m `0d84288b-5014-5b32-4355-9452883f472d` (CadQuery, Apache-2.0).5The source's tooth cutters are boxes centred on Z = 0, so they cut the lower half of6a ring that stands on Z = 0; they are merged into one tool first, as the source makes7a compound of them. A first program

A program is plain Python: import sand3d as s3d, then verbs. Makers take a name and return a solid; edits change it and return it.

A rack docs/examples/rack.py

def rack(n=4, pitch=30, depth=40, t=5):
    base = s3d.extrude("base", s3d.rect(n * pitch, depth, r=3), t)
    pegs = s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("peg", 6, 20), on=s3d.grid(n, 1, pitch), z=t)         # a copy per frame
    hook = s3d.at(s3d.extrude("hook", s3d.rect(4, 12), 12), x=n * pitch / 2 - 4, z=t)
    image = s3d.transform(s3d.copy(hook), mirror="x")                                # its image across x = 0
    s3d.join(base, pegs, hook, image)                                                # a list is its elements
    s3d.hole(base, 4, on=s3d.grid(2, 1, (n - 1) * pitch).move(y=depth / 2 - 6))
    s3d.chamfer(base, 0.6, edges="peg")
    return base

9 lines · 246 tokens (o200k_base)

  • The base is a rounded rectangle, extruded 5 high from z = 0.
  • One peg, placed on each frame of a grid: at returns the copies.
  • A hook, and its image across x = 0 by transform(…, mirror="x").
  • join takes the list of pegs as it is, then two holes and a chamfer on the edges named after the pegs.

Six rules

Learn these 6 and the rest of the API reads by itself.

  1. A placement is a frame plus values. at sets the values it is given and keeps the others; on= changes the frame, and x, y, z then run along its axes; transform moves the whole thing, as a parent would, mirror included.
  2. To repeat, pass a list of frames to on=: once per frame, in at, hole and pocket.
  3. A list of objects is worth its elements, wherever a verb takes objects.
  4. What a verb uses up no longer exists. copy keeps it; always use what at returns.
  5. Every solid starts at z = 0, centred in x and y: box is the extrude of its rect; extrude(both=True) centres one on its plane. A face's frame starts where the origin projects onto it: a vertical face's, at its foot. A frame's Z is the face's normal; on a face whose normal is ±Z its X is +X, on any other X is Z × normal: on a face looking +X, X is +Y and Y is up. A side, an edge or a corner of a box is named by directions: bbox(ob, "+X") is the centre of that side of its bounding box, "+X-Y" the middle of an edge, "+X-Y+Z" a corner, with the axes of a face looking the first way named, on a part or a group; at's anchor takes the same ("-Z", "+Y-Z"; its words top bottom left right front back are +Z -Z -X +X -Y +Y).
  6. A joint lets a part move on another. Place the part first: joint does not move it, it says how it moves — on the part its frame on was read on (ob.face, bbox, local, an assembly's anchor; it stays read on it through .move, .turn, .offset), about or along axis: a direction ("+Z", "-X"…) in the space the parent lives in, as in face, or "normal", on's Z. A pivot given as numbers — a source's joint origin, xyz and rpy — is local(parent, x, y, z, rx, ry, rz), in the parent's own space: at(child, on=…) places the child there, joint hangs it there. Positive values slide along the axis, or turn by the right hand about it: about +Z, +X turns toward +Y — a door hinged on the -Y edge of a +X face opens outward about "-Z". The range contains 0; a joint that follows another takes its range from it. Everything is built at rest, every joint at 0; pose(child, value) moves the mechanism. A part with no joint moves with its group; a jointed part moves by its joint, whatever group it is in; on is never read on the child itself. Joints may come before or after group/assembly. copy copies a jointed part's joints (it hangs on the same parent); transform moves the part with its pivot (a mirror image moves as the image of the motion); at refuses it. Two joints on one child compose in order (a screw: a turn, and a slide that follows it with ratio=pitch / 360).
Two traps. A face's frame starts where the parent's origin projects onto the face. That is the world origin for a part you have placed: on a box moved to x = 100, face("top") starts at x = 0. Build at the origin, read faces, then place; or read bbox(ob, "+Z"), the centre of the side wherever the part is: the frame to hinge on. And join fuses parts that don't touch without a word: they end up as separate pieces of one object.

Profiles

A profile is a flat outline in XY. It is not a solid: it becomes one through extrude, revolve, sweep or loft. Profiles add and subtract with + and -.

Basic shapes

rect(w, d, r=0, chamfer=0)Centred; corners rounded or cut
circle(d)Centred
ellipse(w, d)Centred
slot(l, d)Round-ended slot along X
polygon(n, d)Regular polygon, corner on +X

Every basic shape is centred on its origin. rect takes r= for rounded corners and chamfer= for cut ones.

shapes = [s3d.rect(40, 24, r=5), s3d.rect(40, 24, chamfer=6), s3d.circle(30),
          s3d.ellipse(40, 20), s3d.slot(44, 16), s3d.polygon(6, 32)]
for i, shape in enumerate(shapes):
    s3d.extrude("plate", s3d.at(shape, x=50 * i), 3)

                 (10, 24), s3d.tangent_arc((10, 40)), (0, 40)])

s3d.extrude("bracket", bracket, 3)
s3d.extrude("hook", s3d.at(hook, x=55), 3)
s3d.extrude("blob", s3d.at(blob, x=110, y=5), 3)

offset(p, t)Grown by t
mirror(p, flip='x')Plus its image, flip negated

s3d.extrude("belt", s3d.offset(belt, 4) - belt, 10)
for wheel in wheels:

Solids

A maker takes a name and returns a solid. Every solid starts at z = 0 and goes up, centred in X and Y.

Primitives

box(name, w, d, h)On Z = 0, centred in X and Y
cylinder(name, d, h)Along Z, from Z = 0
tube(name, d, d_in, h)Along Z, from Z = 0
cone(name, d, h, d2=0)Along Z, from Z = 0

wedge(name, w, d, h, top=0)Box narrowed on top
torus(name, d, d_wire)Ring about Z, on Z = 0
dome(name, d, h)Cap on Z = 0

All of them stand on z = 0. cone(d, h, d2) goes from diameter d at the bottom to d2 at the top. torus(d, d_wire): d is the diameter of the wire's centre line. at(parts, on=grid) would put every part on every frame; zip pairs them one to one.

         s3d.cone("cone", 30, 40, d2=10), s3d.sphere("sphere", 30), s3d.wedge("wedge", 40, 20, 30, top=10),
         s3d.torus("torus", 40, 8), s3d.dome("dome", 30, 10)]
for part, place in zip(parts, s3d.grid(4, 2, 50, 60)):   # one part per frame
    s3d.at(part, on=place)

Edits

An edit changes its first argument in place and returns it. Edges and faces are reached by the names the maker gave them: top, bottom, side, rim, cut, the tool's name, or plate.top.

cut, join, intersect

cut(ob, *tools)Subtract tools
join(ob, *others)Fuse others in; ob's material wins: group keeps each its own
intersect(ob, tool)Keep the common part

The tools are used up. A cut that touches nothing raises: it is a mistake, not a no-op.

plate = s3d.box("plate", 60, 40, 8)
s3d.cut(plate, s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("pin", 10, 20), x=10, z=-6),
        s3d.at(s3d.box("notch", 10, 50, 20), x=-30, z=-2))
s3d.join(plate, s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("boss", 16, 10), x=-10, z=7))
s3d.at(s3d.intersect(s3d.box("cube", 30, 30, 30), s3d.at(s3d.sphere("ball", 40), z=-5)), x=70)

Frames and placement

A frame is a place to build on: an origin, a normal (its Z) and an X. Faces, grids, rings and paths give frames; at puts things on them.

ob.face("top") is the frame of a named face, ob.face("+X") the face furthest that way. A frame moves along its own axes (.move), turns (.turn) and offsets along its normal (.offset).

Articulations

A joint says how a part moves on another: on a frame read on the parent (ob.face, bbox, an assembly's anchor), about or along an axis: a direction of the parent's space, or "normal". Everything is built at rest; pose moves the mechanism, and export writes it as a URDF or a GLB nested by its joints. Each scene below is shown posed.

bbox(ob, which)Frame on its bounding box: a side "+X", an edge "+X-Y", a corner "+X-Y+Z"

bbox(ob, "+X") is the centre of that side of the bounding box, "+X-Y" the middle of an edge, "+X-Y+Z" a corner, with the axes of a face looking the first way named: the frame to hinge on. at(anchor=) takes the same directions.

cab = s3d.box("cab", 60, 60, 85)
s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("side", 8, 12), on=s3d.bbox(cab, "+X"))        # the centre of a side
s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("edge", 8, 12), on=s3d.bbox(cab, "+X-Y"))      # the middle of an edge
s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("corner", 8, 12), on=s3d.bbox(cab, "+X-Y+Z"))  # a corner

joint and pose: the four kinds

joint(name, child, on, kind='revolute', axis='normal', range=None, follows=None, ratio=1)How child moves on the part on was read on: revolute (range in degrees), continuous (no range), prismatic (range in the unit), free (no axis, no range); follows: a child or a joint name, and this joint's value is ratio × its (degrees per unit, or units per degree), no range; returns child
pose(ob, value, joint=None)Move the mechanism: that joint to value (degrees or the unit), an error outside its range; what it carries follows; joint= when child has two

A lid revolute on the -Y edge of the top (degrees; the range contains 0), a wheel continuous, a drawer prismatic (the program's unit), a ball free. joint neither moves nor reparents the part; pose moves the mechanism. About +X, +Y turns toward +Z: a positive value lifts the lid.

chest = s3d.box("chest", 500, 400, 300)
lid = s3d.at(s3d.box("lid", 500, 400, 20), z=300)
s3d.joint("lid_hinge", lid, s3d.bbox(chest, "+Z-Y"), axis="+X", range=(0, 110))
wheel = s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("wheel", 160, 30), on=chest.face("+X").move(0, 150))
s3d.joint("wheel_spin", wheel, chest.face("+X").move(0, 150), kind="continuous")
drawer = s3d.at(s3d.box("drawer", 180, 60, 300), on=s3d.bbox(chest, "-Y").move(y=-80).offset(-299))
s3d.seat(chest, drawer)                                  # its bay, cut where it rests
s3d.joint("drawer_slide", drawer, s3d.bbox(chest, "-Y"), kind="prismatic", axis="-Y", range=(0, 250))
ball = s3d.at(s3d.sphere("ball", 60), x=-320)
s3d.joint("ball", ball, chest.face("top"), kind="free")   # no axis, no range, no pose
s3d.pose(lid, 70)
s3d.pose(drawer, 180)

upper = s3d.group("upper", s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("arm", 16, 250), z=348), knuckles[2])

11 lines · 329 tokens (o200k_base)

local: a pivot given as numbers

local(ob, x=0, y=0, z=0, rx=0, ry=0, rz=0)Frame at (x, y, z) of its own space, turned (rx, ry, rz) degrees

local(ob, x, y, z, rx, ry, rz) is the frame at a point of the part's own space, turned as at turns: a source's joint origin, xyz and rpy, as written. One frame places the child (at(on=)) and hangs it (joint); the elbow is read in the arm's own space, wherever the arm stands.

base = s3d.cylinder("base", 160, 20)
shoulder = s3d.local(base, z=20, ry=-30)                     # the arm rises 30° at rest
arm = s3d.at(s3d.group("arm", s3d.at(s3d.box("beam", 300, 30, 30), x=150)), on=shoulder)
s3d.joint("shoulder", arm, shoulder, axis="+Y", range=(-45, 90))
elbow = s3d.local(arm, x=300, rx=90)                         # 300 along the arm, its Z the arm's -Y
hand = s3d.at(s3d.group("hand", s3d.at(s3d.box("rod", 200, 20, 20), x=100)), on=elbow)
s3d.joint("elbow", hand, elbow, axis="normal", range=(-90, 90))
s3d.pose(arm, -20)
s3d.pose(hand, -60)

9 lines · 229 tokens (o200k_base)

copy and mirror a jointed part

The leaf is a group: board and handle weld. copy carries the joint, the copy hangs on the same parent, and its mirror image moves as the image of the motion: both leaves open toward +Y.

post = s3d.at(s3d.box("post", 100, 100, 1500), x=-800)
s3d.transform(s3d.copy(post), mirror="x")
board = s3d.at(s3d.box("board", 750, 40, 1200), x=-375, z=150)
handle = s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("handle", 20, 60), on=s3d.bbox(board, "+Y").move(x=315))
leaf = s3d.group("leaf", board, handle)
s3d.joint("hinge", leaf, s3d.bbox(post, "+X").move(x=20), axis="+Z", range=(0, 90))  # on its +Y edge
twin = s3d.transform(s3d.copy(leaf), mirror="x")
s3d.pose(leaf, 60)
s3d.pose(twin, 60)

9 lines · 204 tokens (o200k_base)

follows and ratio

A joint that follows another takes ratio × its value and no range: a screw cap is a turn and a slide that follows it, 3 mm per turn; a small gear follows a big one at −2.

bottle = s3d.revolve("bottle", [(0, 0), (35, 0), (35, 140), (14, 175), (14, 200), (0, 200)])
cap = s3d.at(s3d.knurl("cap", 36, 24), z=190)
s3d.joint("cap_turn", cap, bottle.face("top"), range=(0, 720))
s3d.joint("cap_lift", cap, bottle.face("top"), kind="prismatic", follows="cap_turn", ratio=3 / 360)
s3d.pose(cap, 720, joint="cap_turn")                      # two turns: 6 mm up
plate = s3d.at(s3d.box("plate", 260, 120, 10), x=250)
big = s3d.at(s3d.gear("big", 30, 3, 12, bore=8), x=200, z=10)
small = s3d.at(s3d.gear("small", 15, 3, 12, bore=8), x=267.5, z=10, rz=12)
s3d.joint("drive", big, plate.face("top").move(200), kind="continuous")     # the face starts at x = 0
s3d.joint("driven", small, plate.face("top").move(267.5), kind="continuous", follows=big, ratio=-2)
s3d.pose(big, 20)

seat: the cavity a part leaves

seat(host, part)Take out of host the volume part fills, as it sits at rest; part untouched

seat(host, part) takes out of the host the volume the part fills at rest and leaves the part as it is: it may move. It cuts the exact shape: a knob turns in a round shank's seat, not a knurled one's.

console = s3d.box("console", 200, 120, 60)
top = console.face("top")
knob = s3d.group("knob", s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("shank", 24, 22), on=top.move(-50).offset(-12)),
                 s3d.at(s3d.knurl("grip", 40, 24), on=top.move(-50).offset(10)))
pin = s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("pin", 16, 60), on=top.move(50).offset(-40))
s3d.seat(console, knob)
s3d.seat(console, pin)
s3d.joint("pin_pull", pin, top.move(50), kind="prismatic", axis="+Z", range=(0, 60))
s3d.pose(pin, 45)                                        # pulled out of its bore

Parts

Ready-made parts, each standing on z = 0.

gear, knurl, thread

gear(name, teeth, module, width, bore=0, angle=20)Involute spur gear
knurl(name, d, h, pitch=None, straight=False)Knurled grip; pitch 1 mm by default
thread(name, d, length, pitch, left=False)Threaded rod

gear(teeth, module, width) is an involute spur gear. knurl is a knurled grip, its pitch 1 mm unless given. thread is an ISO V-thread rod.

Materials

material says what a part is made of: one of 22 presets, its values changed where the call says. It tags the object and never touches its mesh; export writes it into the GLB.

The 22 presets

material(ob, kind, color=None, roughness=None, metallic=None, opacity=None, emission=None)Kind: oak walnut pine birch steel brushed_steel chrome aluminium brass copper painted_metal plastic glossy_plastic rubber glass ceramic fabric velvet leather marble concrete light; color "#rrggbb"

Woods, metals, plastics, rubber, glass, ceramic, soft goods, stone, and light, a surface that gives light in its own colour. A wrong name raises and suggests the nearest one.

kinds = ["oak", "walnut", "pine", "birch", "steel", "brushed_steel", "chrome", "aluminium",
         "brass", "copper", "painted_metal", "plastic", "glossy_plastic", "rubber", "glass",
         "ceramic", "fabric", "velvet", "leather", "marble", "concrete", "light"]
for kind, place in zip(kinds, s3d.grid(6, 4, 80, -100)):
    s3d.material(s3d.at(s3d.sphere(kind, 40), on=place), kind)
    label = s3d.extrude("label", s3d.text(kind, 9), 1)
    s3d.material(s3d.at(label, on=place.move(y=-30)), "rubber")

7 lines · 189 tokens (o200k_base)

On an assembly, and what a call changes

On a group or an assembly, material reaches every part under it that names none of its own: the nearest call wins, in whatever order the calls come. color= ("#rrggbb"), roughness=, metallic=, opacity= and emission= change the preset. The tag follows the part through cut, fillet and copy.

top = s3d.fillet(s3d.box("top", 1400, 800, 32), 3, edges="top")
legs = s3d.at(s3d.box("leg", 60, 60, 718), on=s3d.grid(2, 2, 1260, 660))
table = s3d.assembly("table", s3d.at(top, z=718), legs)
s3d.material(table, "walnut")                            # every part under it
s3d.material(legs, "painted_metal", color="#2f5d50")     # the nearest call wins
vase = s3d.shell(s3d.revolve("vase", [(0, 0), (70, 0), (90, 120), (45, 260), (0, 260)]), 4, open="top")
s3d.material(s3d.at(vase, x=-300, z=750), "glass", color="#3fae6a")
bowl = s3d.shell(s3d.revolve("bowl", [(0, 0), (60, 0), (130, 80), (0, 80)]), 5, open="top")
s3d.material(s3d.at(bowl, x=250, z=750), "ceramic")
s3d.material(s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("cup", 70, 90), x=0, y=200, z=750), "brass")

group, assembly, attach, Handle, export, units, empty_scene, fingerprint

group(name, *children)Parent of children
assembly(name, *children, **anchors)Parts and anchors
attach(handle, name, *children)A detail, under a handle
Handle(root, **anchors)Root and anchors
export(root, path)root and what hangs on it by its joints, in metres: .glb at the current pose, joints in extras; .urdf a link per moving part, at rest, meshes beside it; .usda the URDF's tree as OpenUSD text, with the materials; .obj and .stl its meshes at the current pose
units(name=None)Length unit: "mm" (default), "cm", "m"
empty_scene()Fresh scene
fingerprint()Digest of the source

They are shown at work in Assemblies. export(root, path) writes in metres, whatever the program's unit: a GLB at the current pose, a URDF at rest with its meshes beside it, or USD text (.usda) with the joints and the materials.

Assemblies

Write the plan first, then the details, then the parts. Each detail hangs on the plan's anchors, so deleting it deletes only it.

  1. The top function is the table of contents. It calls the plan, then one line per detail, and returns the root. Someone reading it sees the object's structure before any number.
  2. The plan builds the architecture and publishes anchors. assembly(name, *parts, **anchors) returns a handle. The anchors are what the details need: a width, a height, a frame, a list of spots. Write them once, in the plan.
  3. Each detail is one add_ function. It takes the handle, reads only its anchors, and hangs its parts with attach. Delete its line and nothing else moves. A detail of a detail lives inside it: the buttons are added by add_back.
  4. The parts come last. Each part is a function with named parameters and defaults. It builds at the origin and stands on z = 0. It does not place itself: the plan or the detail that calls it does.
  5. Build at the origin, place last. A face's frame starts where the parent's origin projects onto it. Read faces before you move a part, or compute heights from the anchors, as add_back does with chair.seat_h.
  6. Repeat and mirror with frames. Four legs are at(leg(), on=grid(2, 2, …)). A right side is transform(copy(left), mirror="x").

A chair, and the same plan without its back docs/examples/chair.py

The chair, part by part docs/examples/chair.py

1"""A chair, written as an assembly: the plan first, then the details, then the parts.2 3`chair` reads as a table of contents. `chair_frame` is the plan: the seat on its legs,4and the anchors the details need. Each `add_` function hangs one detail on those5anchors: delete its line and nothing else moves — without `add_back` it is a stool.6The parts come last, each built at its own origin, standing on z = 0.7"""8import sand3d as s3d9 10 11def chair(width=440, depth=420, seat_h=450):12    chair = chair_frame(width, depth, seat_h)   # the plan13    add_back(chair)                             # the details, on the plan's anchors14    add_rails(chair)15    return chair.root16 17 18# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the plan19 20def chair_frame(width, depth, seat_h, t=30, inset=35):21    """The seat on four legs. Publishes the width, the seat's height and the line22    the back stands on."""23    legs = s3d.at(leg(seat_h - t), on=s3d.grid(2, 2, width - 2 * inset, depth - 2 * inset))24    seat = s3d.at(seat_board(width, depth, t), z=seat_h - t)25    return s3d.assembly("chair", seat, legs, width=width, depth=depth, seat_h=seat_h, inset=inset,26                        back_y=depth / 2 - 20)27 28 29# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the details30 31def add_back(chair, h=420, t=24, button_d=16):32    """A panel standing on the seat's back edge, buttoned on its face."""33    back = s3d.at(back_panel(chair.width - 40, h, t), y=chair.back_y, z=chair.seat_h)34    # a side face's frame starts at z = 0, below the parent's origin, and its Y is up35    face = back.face("-Y").move(y=chair.seat_h + h * 0.6)36    buttons = s3d.at(s3d.dome("button", button_d, 5), on=s3d.grid(3, 2, 100, 110, on=face))37    s3d.attach(chair, "back", back, buttons)38 39 40def add_rails(chair, d=18, z=160):41    """A rail between the front and back legs, on each side."""42    # both=True: centred on its middle, so turned about X it spans the depth evenly43    rail = s3d.extrude("rail", s3d.circle(d), chair.depth - 2 * chair.inset, both=True)44    sides = s3d.grid(2, 1, chair.width - 2 * chair.inset, on=s3d.Frame((0, 0, z)))45    s3d.attach(chair, "rails", s3d.at(rail, rx=90, on=sides))46 47 48# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the parts49 50def seat_board(width, depth, t):51    return s3d.fillet(s3d.box("seat", width, depth, t), 8, edges="top")52 53 54def leg(h, foot=26, top=36):55    """Tapered, its foot on z = 0."""56    return s3d.cone("leg", foot, h, d2=top)57 58 59def back_panel(width, h, t):60    return s3d.fillet(s3d.box("back", width, t, h), 6, edges="top")

1import sand3d as s3d2 3 4def lamp(stem_h=300):5    base = s3d.revolve("base", [(0, 0), (70, 0), (60, 20), (0, 20)])6    stem = s3d.at(s3d.cylinder("stem", 12, stem_h), on=base.face("top"))7    lamp = s3d.assembly("lamp", base, stem, head=s3d.Frame((0, 0, 20 + stem_h)))8    add_shade(lamp)9    return lamp10 11 12def add_shade(lamp, d=180):13    shade = s3d.shell(s3d.cone("shade", d, 120, d2=d / 2), 1.5, open="top bottom")14    s3d.attach(lamp, "shade", s3d.at(shade, on=lamp.head))

The same structure, at full scale programs/tufted_chair.py

A buttoned back rolling over at the top, a domed seat on a nailed apron, four tapered legs. The architecture is the seat on its legs; the back and every row of trim are details; the parts come last, in the order they are called. The legs are lofts through their sections, the right ones images of the left.

1"""A tufted chair: a buttoned back rolling over at the top, a domed seat on a nailed2apron, four tapered legs.3 4Millimetres, Z up, the chair's front towards -Y; built as its left half's legs, the5right ones mirrored. The architecture is the seat on its legs; the back and every6row of trim are details added to it: deleting `add_back` leaves a stool, and the7back's tufts follow the width they are given.8"""9import json10import math11import sys12 13import sand3d as s3d14 15 16def tufted_chair(width=520):17    chair = chair_frame(width)18    add_back(chair)19    add_seat_nails(chair)20    return chair.root21 22 23def chair_frame(width=520, depth=480, seat_z=430, inset=50, floor=0):24    seat = upholstered_seat(width, depth)25    legs = []26    for leg, y in ((front_leg, -(depth / 2 - inset)), (rear_leg, depth / 2 - inset)):27        left = s3d.at(leg(), x=-(width / 2 - inset), y=y, z=floor)28        legs += [left, s3d.transform(s3d.copy(left), mirror="x")]   # the right one: its image across x = 029 39 40def add_seat_nails(chair, pitch=22, d=10, h=5):41    """One nail every `pitch` along the seat's seam, round its front and sides."""42    seat = chair.seat43    spots = s3d.snap(seat.parts, face, where its cover is nailed to the frame,53    from (x, z) to (x, z), found from in front, `reach` away."""54    spots = []55    for side in (-1, 1):56        (x0, z0), (x1, z1) = face57 *[s3d.at(s3d.dome("nail", d, h), on=f) for f in spots])60 61 62# ---------------------------------------------------------------- parts, in the order they are called63 64def section(z, w, d, x=0, y=0, n=2, taper=0):65    """One cross-section of a loft: a superellipse `w` wide and `d` deep, squareness66    `n` (2 an ellipse, 4 a box with round corners), its +Y side narrowed by `taper`,67    centred at (x, y, z)."""68    return s3d.at(s3d.superellipse(w, d, n, taper), x=x, y=y, z=z)69 70 71def upholstered_seat(width=520, depth=480, taper=0.04, squareness=6, board=-8,72                     crown=((15, 3, 3, 0), (35, 12, 10, 4), (55, 30, 24, 8), (68, 90, 72, 12), (76, 190, 160, 18)),73                     apron=60, dip=15, wall=8, seam_up=6, seam_out=10):74    """A cushion domed over a board, an apron hanging round it. `crown` is the dome,75    level by level: (height, inset at the sides, inset front and back, shift back)."""76    w = width / (1 + taper)  # the loft's mean width; the front edge is `width`77    cushion = s3d.loft("cushion", section(board, w, depth, n=squareness, taper=taper),78                       *[section(z, w - 2 * side, depth - 2 * end, y=back, n=squareness, taper=taper)79                         for z, side, end, back in crown])80 81    def drop(x):  # how far the apron hangs below the board: deepest mid-front82        return apron + dip * math.cos(math.pi * x / width) ** 283 84    hem = s3d.superellipse(w - wall, depth - wall, squareness, taper).loops[0].pts85    skirt = s3d.loft("apron", *[s3d.at(s3d.superellipse(drop(x), wall, squareness), x=x, y=y, z=board - drop(x) / 2,86                                       ry=-90) for x, y in hem], follow=True, loop=True)87    # the seam the nails follow: just outside the apron, round the front and sides88    # but not the back, which the back of the chair covers — from the middle of the back round89    rim = s3d.superellipse(w + 2 * seam_out, depth + 2 * seam_out, squareness, 36), (420, 0, 44, 44))):96    """A square leg with round corners, tapering to its foot, which steps forward.97    `profile` is (z, y, width, depth) from the floor up; its origin is under its 102def rear_leg(height=420, profile=((0, 16, 30, 30), (210, 6, 36, 36), (420, 0, 44, 44))):103    """The back leg, raking back to its foot. Its origin is under its foot."""104    body = s3d.loft("rear_leg", *[section(z * height / profile[-1][0], w, d, y=y, n=4) for z, y, w, d in profile])105    return s3d.group("rear_leg", s3d.at(body, y=-profile[0][1]))106 107 108def tufted_back(width=520, drawn_for=520, squareness=4, profile=(109        (-260, 0, 440, 50),    # foot, behind the seat: z, y, width, depth110        (-140, 6, 460, 60),111        (-20, 14, 470, 64),    # the cushioned middle112        (90, 24, 480, 66),113        (170, 36, 490, 72),    # leaning back114        (205, 58, 490, 70),    # over the top115        (180, 82, 490, 60),    # down the back116        (130, 88, 490, 46)),   # tucked under117        tuft_rows=((-60, -120), (-52, -40), (-44, 40), (-34, 120)), tuft_pitch=80, tuft_margin=100, tuft_r=55,118        tuft_depth=20):119    """A cushioned panel rising from the seat and rolling over backwards, one loft120    along its own centre line; buttoned on a diamond lattice, each tuft row (y, z),121    the rows' columns staggered. Limits

  • The renders show shape, not tolerance: Blender's Workbench engine, orthographic. The scenes that set materials are rendered by Cycles, under a plain sky; another renderer will light them its own way.
  • Two words for one idea: wire closes its path with closed=, loft its ring with loop=.
  • The API reference a model reads is docs/api.md, 3,643 tokens (o200k_base). This page is for people.
